- Urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) or 24-hour urine protein — essential to confirm nephrotic-range proteinuria (>3.5 g/day or UPCR >3500 mg/g).  
- Renal ultrasound — needed to exclude structural disease or chronic changes inconsistent with MCD (e.g., small kidneys, scarring).  
- Anti-PLA2R antibodies — to rule out primary membranous nephropathy, a key mimic in adults.  
- Serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation — to exclude monoclonal gammopathy-associated disease (e.g., AL amyloidosis, MGRS).  
- Complement levels (C3/C4) and ANA — to exclude lupus nephritis or MPGN variants.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Minimal Change Disease
